review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–153) from the supplied text. I did not open any other source files. It has three theorems. (1) `exists_measure_continuity_modulus_le` goes from compact sets to a modulus: compact sets of curves are uniformly equicontinuous, so they miss the bad event. (2) `isTightMeasureSet_of_map_eval_of_continuity_modulus` goes the other way. It builds a compact closure from countably many bad events, using Arzelà–Ascoli. (3) The iff theorem only combines (1), (2) and `hS.map`. Theorems (1) and (2) run in opposite directions and share no nontrivial reasoning. The uniform-equicontinuity step in (1) uses existing Mathlib lemmas, and (2) constructs equicontinuity from the modulus directly. The repeated pieces are `isTightMeasureSet_iff_exists_isCompact_measure_compl_le.mp` and the bad-event set `{γ | ∃ s t, dist s t < δ ∧ η ≤ dist (γ s) (γ t)}`. Both are short statements or calls to existing API, not reasoning. Introducing a shared lemma or a named definition for the bad event would be a thin abbreviation and would not meet the rubric's bar. Inside (2), the two `mem_iUnion.mpr` membership steps are routine unfolding. I found no justified finding.
